affected_locations: Low- and lower middle-income countries (LICs and LMICs)
key_impacts: Nearly 4.2 million COVID-19 cases and 284,000 deaths reported globally as of 11 May 2020.
Worst-affected countries at that time were in Europe and North America.
COVID-19 epidemics can rapidly exceed healthcare capacity, even in high-income countries such as the United States and Italy.

Modeling in the report estimates a 32.0% (2.5th–97.5th: 8.0%–72.5%) higher probability of death in the poorest wealth quintile compared to the wealthiest due to differences in handwashing access, occupation, and hospital access.

An estimated 2.01 (1.89–2.13) billion people lack access to handwashing facilities globally; in 22 of 26 LMIC countries assessed, less than 25% of households in the poorest quintile had soap and water at home, limiting infection-prevention.
